newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedbank details Foreningsbanken merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Swedbank details Foreningsbanken merger plan.

text.p: Sweden's Swedbank said on Tuesday it will offer two new shares in a merged bank for every seven Foreningsbanken A shares.
Swedbank said the merger with Foreningsbanken would give at least 1.5 billion crowns in savings from 2000 and at least 2,000 staff of the combined 14,000 staff in the two banks would be cut.
Swedbank and Foreningsbanken said at a news conference announcing the merger that restructuring costs would be around 2.0 billion crowns at most.
The bank also said its property unit Mandamus would be distributed to the merged bank's shareholders in 1998.
Main shareholders support the merger, the bank said. Foreningsbanken's main owners, farmers' associations holding around 20 percent, have previously opposed approaches from Swedbank.
The new bank aims to pay a dividend of 30 percent of pre-tax profit in the long-term.
Swedbank's chairman Goran Collert will be appointed chairman and Swedbank's current chief executive Reinhold Geijer will become managing director of the new bank, to be called ForeningsSparbank.

Foreningsbanken's chairman, Bo Dockered, who is also head of the country's main farmers' association LRF, will become vice chairman and the bank's chief executive Bo Soderberg will become deputy managing director.

The merged bank will have about five million customers, a market capitalisation of 42 billion crowns, an operating profit of about 6.4 billion crowns, lending of 470 billion crowns and a capital adequacy ratio of 12.8 percent at the start of 1997.
The bank will be called ForeningsbankenSparbanken AB. Swedbank is called Sparbanken in Swedish.

"The boards think that a merger on an equal basis between Foreningsbanken and Swedbank is a logical and necessary step to create a long-term strong and efficient bank for the next century," the banks said.
The bank will be able to take advantage of significant cost cutting and a stronger market position, but initially there will be costs connected with the restructuring, the banks said.

"The stronger market position means ForeningsbankenSparbanken will have good growth opportunities," the bank said. "The merger creates prerequisites for a better return for shareholders and increased dividend capacity."

The deal is conditional on more than 90 percent of Foreningsbanken's shareholders accepting it, while Swedbank will see the deal through also if fewer than 90 percent of its shareholders accept the bid, the banks said.
The banks will publish a prospectus on April 11 and the offering period will span from April 15 to May 15.
Swedbank will hold its annual shareholders' meeting on April 23 and Foreningsbanken will have its meeting on April 29.
The merger will be implemented when all licenses have been obtained, the banks said.
